description: Monitor a website: HookPulse calls check.url every interval_sec (default 300) and alerts when it goes down and when it is back. Read billing before a paid option. A charged request returns HTTP 402. With `check` the monitor is a site: HookPulse calls `check.url` every `interval_sec` (default 300) and alerts when it goes down — two failed checks in a row, one minute apart, from a server whose own connection is proven — and when it answers again. `{"check":{"url":"https://example.com/"}}` is enough; the name defaults to the host. A site has no `cron`, no `max_duration_sec` and no ingest URL. This response is the only one that shows the monitor's `token` and the `templates` — keep them. The second monitor, or an interval below the free minimum, answers **402 with `accepts[]`**: pay and repeat. A miss alerts at most once per 24h — or per `alert_repeat_sec`, or per interval, whichever is longer. Send `cron`+`tz`+`grace_sec` instead of `interval_sec` for a real schedule: a 03:00 backup is late at 03:01:30, not 24 hours later. `max_duration_sec` catches the other failure: a run that starts and hangs, which plain silence detection only notices at the next scheduled time.

alert_to.description: E-mail to alert on a miss; without it, the account is alerted.

alert_url.description: Public HTTPS URL that receives a POST on a miss (Slack Incoming, Discord, n8n).

check.description: url (http/https, public; required), method (GET or HEAD), expect_status (200-399 by default, a range a-b or one code), keyword (text that must be on the page), timeout_ms (1000..30000)

name.description: how you will recognise the site in an alert; default: its host

paused_until.description: maintenance window end (UTC ISO), max 30 days ahead

tags.description: Up to 8 tags to group this monitor: lower-case letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 32 characters each. A comma-separated string works too. We lower-case and de-duplicate, so `Prod` and `prod` are the same tag.
